items.title: Write Briar Glen environment concepts prompts (11 assets)
items.description:
## Why
Briar Glen is the first playable area and the "one warm room, one uneasy thing" tone target (style bible §2.2); every town texture, prop and light is judged against these paintings.

## What
Write one prompt file per asset in `assets/prompts/environment/<asset-id>.md` (category: environment) from template `environment-concept.md`, with the GPT STYLE PREAMBLE (style bible §14) plus its §14.1 category add-on pasted verbatim, the output spec, the bible consistency checklist, consuming bead(s) and an empty iteration log.

Eye-level third-person concept paintings for the Market Green (notice board, the Sleeping Ox, the Lamplit Stacks leaning on Brand's Forge, Vane House on the rise), the town at night with Tansy sleepwalking, and the key interiors: inn common room, three-storey bookshop, forge (bell mould on the wall), Fletchery & Simples, the bakery at 4 a.m., Watch House jail with loose drain stone, Vane House exterior and study, and the Glen Well shaft down to the flooded Vesperine cistern.

Asset ids (11):
- `env-briar-glen-market-green-01`
- `env-briar-glen-night-01`
- `env-sleeping-ox-common-room-01`
- `env-lamplit-stacks-interior-01`
- `env-brand-forge-interior-01`
- `env-fenn-fletchery-interior-01`
- `env-pell-bakery-interior-01`
- `env-watch-house-jail-01`
- `env-vane-house-exterior-01`
- `env-vane-house-study-01`
- `env-glen-well-cistern-01`

## Scope
- In: One prompt file per asset id above
- In: Consuming bead references and anchor/reference inputs (our own approved assets only)
- In: Output spec per template
- Out: Running the generator (see `e37-asset-env-town-concepts-generate`)
- Out: Changing a preamble (bible bead + version bump only)

## Notes
Also consumed as mood targets by `e24-first-night`, `e24-sleeping-ox`, `e24-lamplit-stacks`, `e24-trade-row`, `e24-watch-house-jail`, `e24-vane-house`, `e24-glen-well-cistern`. The night concept shows Tansy as a sleepwalker (nightclothes, barefoot, eyes open, serene — style bible §5.2). These concepts become reference inputs for the town texture, prop and sky sets.

Prompts cite the locked style anchors from `e37-asset-style-lock` as reference inputs. Canon names and details follow `docs/narrative/story-bible.md`.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the 11 asset ids listed in this bead, when the asset validator runs over `assets/prompts/`, then every id has exactly one prompt file whose asset id equals its filename stem and passes naming checks (`<category>-<subject>-<variant>`, ≤ 64 chars).
- AC-2 [content] Given each prompt file, when the validator compares its preamble block with docs/art/style-bible.md §14, then it matches byte-for-byte and the correct §14.1 category add-on follows it.
- AC-3 [content] Given each prompt file, when inspected, then it names its consuming bead(s), output spec (16:9, 1536×864 generate, PNG, painterly concept — reference/mood target for grey-box and art-dress, not a runtime texture) and the filled consistency checklist, with no unfilled `<…>` placeholders.
- AC-4 [content] Given the set, when reviewed against the bible, then every prompt writes out the palette hexes, shape language and silhouette rules needed to meet the approval criterion: each painting reads as Briar Glen golden-hour/lantern palette (thatch #C9A66B, plaster #EADFC8, lantern #FFB85C), shows its gameplay affordances (hiding spots, climbable routes, the loose drain stone, the well rung) and carries one uneasy detail without horror.
- AC-5 [content] Edge: given a prompt that asks for text/letters, names an artist, studio or game, uses a non-canon name for a story-bible subject, or contains an API key pattern, when the validator runs, then it fails and names the file and line.

items.title: Generate Briar Glen environment concepts via Codex CLI
items.description:
## Why
Claude produces every image candidate so the owner only has to approve (contract §6).

## What
Run `e37-image-gen-runner` (`codex exec` → gpt-image; fallback OpenAI Images API) for all 11 prompt files of `e37-asset-env-town-concepts-prompts`. Outputs land in `assets/_incoming/<asset-id>/vN.png` with a `vN.json` sidecar; Claude self-checks each candidate against its checklist, iterates, logs every iteration, then builds a batch review page for the owner.

## Scope
- In: Batch generation in planned batches respecting subscription limits
- In: Self-check + iteration log per asset
- In: Batch review page (contact sheet) for the approval bead
- Out: Owner approval (`e37-asset-env-town-concepts-approve`)
- Out: Committing final assets (integrate bead)

## Notes
Output spec: 16:9, 1536×864 generate, PNG, painterly concept — reference/mood target for grey-box and art-dress, not a runtime texture. Record account tier in every sidecar — restrictive-tier outputs are placeholders only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the 11 prompt files, when the runner batch completes, then `assets/_incoming/<asset-id>/vN.png` and a `vN.json` sidecar (prompt path, tool, model, account tier, date) exist for every id.
- AC-2 [content] Given each candidate, when checked against its output spec (16:9, 1536×864 generate, PNG, painterly concept — reference/mood target for grey-box and art-dress, not a runtime texture), then dimensions, transparency/background and layout match or the iteration log records why it was regenerated.
- AC-3 [content] Given the batch review page, when opened, then it shows every id with its latest version, the prompt path and the checklist result.
- AC-4 [integration] Edge: given the image runner hits a usage/rate limit or network error mid-batch, when the batch is re-run, then it resumes from the first id without a candidate, never regenerates an id that already has a candidate or an approval record, and logs the back-off without printing any API key.
- AC-5 [integration] Given all sidecars and iteration logs, when the secret scanner runs, then no API key or token is found.

items.title: Owner approval: Briar Glen environment concepts
items.description:
## Why
Every shipped asset needs an owner decision at the image gate; CI refuses final assets without one (contract §6).

## What
The owner reviews the batch review page of 11 candidates and approves or rejects each item with a note. Claude records every decision in `assets/approvals.json` (asset id, gate: image, version, SHA-256, approver, date, notes). Rejected items loop back to `e37-asset-env-town-concepts-generate` with the note appended to their iteration log.

## Scope
- In: Owner decision per asset
- In: Approval records written by Claude
- In: Re-queue of rejected items
- Out: Generation or editing by the owner — the owner never edits assets

## Notes
Approval criteria: each painting reads as Briar Glen golden-hour/lantern palette (thatch #C9A66B, plaster #EADFC8, lantern #FFB85C), shows its gameplay affordances (hiding spots, climbable routes, the loose drain stone, the well rung) and carries one uneasy detail without horror. Batch reviews are designed to take ≤ 15 minutes of owner time.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the review page, when the owner finishes the session, then each of the 11 ids has an approve or reject decision with notes recorded in `assets/approvals.json` for gate "image".
- AC-2 [manual] Given the approved items viewed side by side, when the owner compares them, then each painting reads as Briar Glen golden-hour/lantern palette (thatch #C9A66B, plaster #EADFC8, lantern #FFB85C), shows its gameplay affordances (hiding spots, climbable routes, the loose drain stone, the well rung) and carries one uneasy detail without horror.
- AC-3 [integration] Edge: given a rejected id, when its decision is recorded, then it is re-queued for `e37-asset-env-town-concepts-generate` with the owner note in its iteration log, and no already-approved id is regenerated.
- AC-4 [integration] Given an approval record whose SHA-256 does not match the file promoted to `assets/source/`, when CI runs, then the approval check fails naming the id.

items.title: Integrate approved Briar Glen environment concepts
items.description:
## Why
Approved environment concepts are the art-dress target: the art-dress, lighting and style-consistency beads compare in-engine screenshots against them.

## What
Promote approved versions to `assets/source/environment/<asset-id>/`, add `assets/CREDITS.md` rows and approval records, register each concept as the `artReference` of its area in the area content data, and add it to the art-dress checklist and `e37-style-consistency-review` comparison sheet.

## Scope
- In: Source promotion, CREDITS rows + approval records in the same commit
- In: Area `artReference` entries and the art-dress comparison sheet
- Out: Art-dressing the areas (art-dress beads); concepts are not runtime assets

## Notes
Consumers: `e24-town-greybox`. Art-dress / lighting-audio beads that wait on this integrate (top-level edges): `e24-town-art-dress`.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the approved sources, when `e37-asset-validator` runs, then every id has a source folder, CREDITS row and a matching approval hash, and the validator is green.
- AC-2 [content] Given `assets/CREDITS.md`, when audited, then each id has a row with tool, model, account tier, date, prompt path and terms URL.
- AC-3 [content] Given the area content data for Briar Glen, when schema-validated, then each area in this set names its concept id in `artReference` and the id resolves to an approved asset.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the art-dress comparison sheet generator, when it runs, then each concept is paired with the latest Playwright screenshot of its area from the same camera preset.
- AC-5 [integration] Edge: given an area whose `artReference` points at an id without an approval record, when CI runs, then the content check fails naming the area and id.

items.title: Write Briarwood and Mooring's Watch concepts prompts (8 assets)

items.title: Write Deepworks and Bellhollow Priory concepts prompts (8 assets)
items.description:
## Why
The Deepworks (lantern pools in the dark) and Bellhollow Priory (melancholy god-rays) are the two dungeon approaches; their contrast carries the Act II mood.

## What
Write one prompt file per asset in `assets/prompts/environment/<asset-id>.md` (category: environment) from template `environment-concept.md`, with the GPT STYLE PREAMBLE (style bible §14) plus its §14.1 category add-on pasted verbatim, the output spec, the bible consistency checklist, consuming bead(s) and an empty iteration log.

Deepworks winch house and cage lift; the ore-sorting hall turned Rootcellar camp (kettle throne, hammocks, Duggan's crate); Vane's sealed gallery with pried Hornfolk carvings and the breach; Bellhollow's roofless nave with god-rays and ivy; the choir of singing-monk statues and hidden choir door; the ruined scriptorium; the belfry with the cracked, tongueless Vesper Bell over the Sounding Shaft; the priory garden with the dead pear tree (plus a bloom variant as a second view in the same file).

Asset ids (8):
- `env-deepworks-winch-house-01`
- `env-deepworks-goblin-hall-01`
- `env-deepworks-sealed-gallery-01`
- `env-bellhollow-nave-01`
- `env-bellhollow-choir-01`
- `env-bellhollow-scriptorium-01`
- `env-bellhollow-belfry-01`
- `env-bellhollow-garden-pear-01`

## Scope
- In: One prompt file per asset id above
- In: Consuming bead references and anchor/reference inputs (our own approved assets only)
- In: Output spec per template
- Out: Running the generator (see `e37-asset-env-mine-priory-concepts-generate`)
- Out: Changing a preamble (bible bead + version bump only)

items.title: Write Knot environment concepts prompts (7 assets)
items.description:
## Why
The Knot is the MVP's heart: cold rune-carved basalt, then the warm Fold reveal that Horn is not a monster, then the dreamlike Cradle (story bible §3.5, style bible §2.2).

## What
Write one prompt file per asset in `assets/prompts/environment/<asset-id>.md` (category: environment) from template `environment-concept.md`, with the GPT STYLE PREAMBLE (style bible §14) plus its §14.1 category add-on pasted verbatim, the output spec, the bible consistency checklist, consuming bead(s) and an empty iteration log.

Outer Ring rune-banded basalt corridors with loom-spider webs copying the runes; the Ossuary bone galleries and Clatter's pale mushroom garden; the Chapel of Echoes with bells and the counterweighted portcullis; Horn's Hall arena; **the Fold** (warm moss beds, sleepers breathing, goblin bread, chalk tallies, skylight — the warm exception); the Sounding Shaft with bell-ropes, counterweights and ledges; **the Cradle** (round chamber, carved faces turned inward, dream-leak, the abbot's warm anchor lanterns the only warm light, the Nightjar only suggested).

Asset ids (7):
- `env-knot-outer-ring-01`
- `env-knot-ossuary-01`
- `env-knot-chapel-echoes-01`
- `env-knot-horns-hall-01`
- `env-knot-fold-01`
- `env-knot-sounding-shaft-01`
- `env-knot-cradle-01`

## Scope
- In: One prompt file per asset id above
- In: Consuming bead references and anchor/reference inputs (our own approved assets only)
- In: Output spec per template
- Out: Running the generator (see `e37-asset-env-knot-concepts-generate`)
- Out: Changing a preamble (bible bead + version bump only)

## Notes
Asset id `env-knot-fold-01` follows the style bible §15.1 example (the world needs list said `env-knot-the-fold-01`). Also consumed as mood targets by `e26-ossuary-galleries`, `e26-chapel-of-echoes`, `e26-horns-hall-fold`, `e26-sounding-shaft-climb`, `e26-cradle-arena`.

Prompts cite the locked style anchors from `e37-asset-style-lock` as reference inputs. Canon names and details follow `docs/narrative/story-bible.md`.

items.title: Generate Knot environment concepts via Codex CLI
items.description:
## Why
Claude produces every image candidate so the owner only has to approve (contract §6).

## What

Outputs land in `assets/_incoming/<asset-id>/vN.png` with a `vN.json` sidecar; Claude self-checks each candidate against its checklist, iterates, logs every iteration, then builds a batch review page for the owner.

## Scope
- In: Batch generation in planned batches respecting subscription limits
- In: Self-check + iteration log per asset
- In: Batch review page (contact sheet) for the approval bead
- Out: Owner approval (`e37-asset-env-knot-concepts-approve`)
- Out: Committing final assets (integrate bead)

## Notes
Output spec: 16:9, 1536×864 generate, PNG, painterly concept — reference/mood target for grey-box and art-dress, not a runtime texture. Record account tier in every sidecar — restrictive-tier outputs are placeholders only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the 7 prompt files, when the runner batch completes, then `assets/_incoming/<asset-id>/vN.png` and a `vN.json` sidecar (prompt path, tool, model, account tier, date) exist for every id.
- AC-2 [content] Given each candidate, when checked against its output spec (16:9, 1536×864 generate, PNG, painterly concept — reference/mood target for grey-box and art-dress, not a runtime texture), then dimensions, transparency/background and layout match or the iteration log records why it was regenerated.
- AC-3 [content] Given the batch review page, when opened, then it shows every id with its latest version, the prompt path and the checklist result.

items.title: Generate Briarwood and Mooring's Watch tileables via Codex CLI
items.description:
## Why
Claude produces every image candidate so the owner only has to approve (contract §6).

## What
Run `e37-image-gen-runner` (`codex exec` → gpt-image; fallback OpenAI Images API) for all 9 prompt files of `e37-asset-tex-wilds-prompts`. Outputs land in `assets/_incoming/<asset-id>/vN.png` with a `vN.json` sidecar; Claude self-checks each candidate against its checklist, iterates, logs every iteration, then builds a batch review page for the owner.

## Scope
- In: Batch generation in planned batches respecting subscription limits
- In: Self-check + iteration log per asset
- In: Batch review page (contact sheet) for the approval bead
- Out: Owner approval (`e37-asset-tex-wilds-approve`)
- Out: Committing final assets (integrate bead)

## Notes
Output spec: 1024² generate (1536² for large ground/wall surfaces) → 1024²/512² KTX2 ETC1S with mips, seamless on both axes, low-contrast edges, plus vertex-colour blend variant; trims 1024×256; decals alpha. Record account tier in every sidecar — restrictive-tier outputs are placeholders only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the 9 prompt files, when the runner batch completes, then `assets/_incoming/<asset-id>/vN.png` and a `vN.json` sidecar (prompt path, tool, model, account tier, date) exist for every id.

- AC-3 [content] Given the batch review page, when opened, then it shows every id with its latest version, the prompt path and the checklist result.

## Why
Every shipped asset needs an owner decision at the image gate; CI refuses final assets without one (contract §6).

- Out: Generation or editing by the owner — the owner never edits assets

items.title: Write location skies and backdrops prompts (4 assets)
items.description:
## Why
Sky and distant backdrop set time-of-day for the whole surface: golden-hour town, night with the song on still nights, overcast forest, and the ending dawn.

## What
Write one prompt file per asset in `assets/prompts/sky/<asset-id>.md` (category: sky) from template `skybox-backdrop.md`, with the GPT STYLE PREAMBLE (style bible §14) plus its §14.1 category add-on pasted verbatim, the output spec, the bible consistency checklist, consuming bead(s) and an empty iteration log.

Briar Glen golden hour, Briar Glen night (moon, no aurora), Briarwood overcast, and the valley dawn used by the endings.

Asset ids (4):
- `sky-briar-glen-golden-hour-01`
- `sky-briar-glen-night-01`
- `sky-briarwood-overcast-01`
- `sky-valley-dawn-01`

## Scope
- In: One prompt file per asset id above
- In: Consuming bead references and anchor/reference inputs (our own approved assets only)
- In: Output spec per template
- Out: Running the generator (see `e37-asset-skies-generate`)
- Out: Changing a preamble (bible bead + version bump only)

## Notes
`sky-valley-dawn-01` is also consumed by `e26-ending-states` (epilogue); it is not linked here so the surface lighting beads do not wait on the finale.

Prompts cite the locked style anchors from `e37-asset-style-lock` as reference inputs. Canon names and details follow `docs/narrative/story-bible.md`.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the 4 asset ids listed in this bead, when the asset validator runs over `assets/prompts/`, then every id has exactly one prompt file whose asset id equals its filename stem and passes naming checks (`<category>-<subject>-<variant>`, ≤ 64 chars).
- AC-2 [content] Given each prompt file, when the validator compares its preamble block with docs/art/style-bible.md §14, then it matches byte-for-byte and the correct §14.1 category add-on follows it.
- AC-3 [content] Given each prompt file, when inspected, then it names its consuming bead(s), output spec (equirect 4096×2048 generate → KTX2 4096×2048 (High) / 2048×1024 (Low), seamless left-right wrap, horizon at vertical centre) and the filled consistency checklist, with no unfilled `<…>` placeholders.
- AC-4 [content] Given the set, when reviewed against the bible, then every prompt writes out the palette hexes, shape language and silhouette rules needed to meet the approval criterion: each sky wraps without a visible seam, matches the location light/mood column of style bible §2.2, and the night sky is dark enough that lantern light remains the key light.
- AC-5 [content] Edge: given a prompt that asks for text/letters, names an artist, studio or game, uses a non-canon name for a story-bible subject, or contains an API key pattern, when the validator runs, then it fails and names the file and line.

items.title: Generate location skies and backdrops via Codex CLI
items.description:
## Why
Claude produces every image candidate so the owner only has to approve (contract §6).

## What
Run `e37-image-gen-runner` (`codex exec` → gpt-image; fallback OpenAI Images API) for all 4 prompt files of `e37-asset-skies-prompts`. Outputs land in `assets/_incoming/<asset-id>/vN.png` with a `vN.json` sidecar; Claude self-checks each candidate against its checklist, iterates, logs every iteration, then builds a batch review page for the owner.

## Scope
- In: Batch generation in planned batches respecting subscription limits
- In: Self-check + iteration log per asset
- In: Batch review page (contact sheet) for the approval bead
- Out: Owner approval (`e37-asset-skies-approve`)
- Out: Committing final assets (integrate bead)

## Notes
Output spec: equirect 4096×2048 generate → KTX2 4096×2048 (High) / 2048×1024 (Low), seamless left-right wrap, horizon at vertical centre. Record account tier in every sidecar — restrictive-tier outputs are placeholders only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the 4 prompt files, when the runner batch completes, then `assets/_incoming/<asset-id>/vN.png` and a `vN.json` sidecar (prompt path, tool, model, account tier, date) exist for every id.
- AC-2 [content] Given each candidate, when checked against its output spec (equirect 4096×2048 generate → KTX2 4096×2048 (High) / 2048×1024 (Low), seamless left-right wrap, horizon at vertical centre), then dimensions, transparency/background and layout match or the iteration log records why it was regenerated.
- AC-3 [content] Given the batch review page, when opened, then it shows every id with its latest version, the prompt path and the checklist result.
- AC-4 [integration] Edge: given the image runner hits a usage/rate limit or network error mid-batch, when the batch is re-run, then it resumes from the first id without a candidate, never regenerates an id that already has a candidate or an approval record, and logs the back-off without printing any API key.
- AC-5 [integration] Given all sidecars and iteration logs, when the secret scanner runs, then no API key or token is found.

items.title: Owner approval: location skies and backdrops
items.description:
## Why
Every shipped asset needs an owner decision at the image gate; CI refuses final assets without one (contract §6).

## What
The owner reviews the batch review page of 4 candidates and approves or rejects each item with a note. Rejected items loop back to `e37-asset-skies-generate` with the note appended to their iteration log.

## Scope
- In: Owner decision per asset
- In: Approval records written by Claude
- In: Re-queue of rejected items
- Out: Generation or editing by the owner — the owner never edits assets

## Notes
Approval criteria: each sky wraps without a visible seam, matches the location light/mood column of style bible §2.2, and the night sky is dark enough that lantern light remains the key light. Batch reviews are designed to take ≤ 15 minutes of owner time.

## Why

items.title: Write bestiary creatures concept prompts (7 images)
items.description:
## Why
Five creature types make up the systemic bestiary: each has a property the world can exploit (fire, light, noise, feeding) that its silhouette must advertise.

## What
Write one prompt file per concept image in `assets/prompts/<category>/<asset-id>.md` (category: creature) from `creature-reference-sheet.md`, flat front-facing on plain parchment so the image-to-3D API gets clean input, with the GPT STYLE PREAMBLE (style bible §14) verbatim, output spec and consistency checklist.

Briar Wolf (lean grey horizontal wedge, silent, ears toward the mine); Hollow Sentinel (Mooring's garrison armour with glowing seams and barony tabard remnants); Loom Spider (pale, dog-sized, radial leg spikes, one ember warning colour); Tallow Ooze (wax blob with wicks, candle stubs and a snuffer visible inside) plus small, puddle and frozen variants; book, lectern and chest mimics, each an almost-perfect object with one tell.

Concept image ids (7):
- `creature-briar-wolf-01`
- `creature-hollow-sentinel-01`
- `creature-loom-spider-01`
- `creature-tallow-ooze-01`
- `creature-mimic-book-01`
- `creature-mimic-lectern-01`
- `creature-mimic-chest-01`

Target model ids (10):
- `model-creature-briar-wolf-01`
- `model-creature-hollow-sentinel-01`
- `model-creature-loom-spider-01`
- `model-creature-tallow-ooze-01`
- `model-creature-tallow-ooze-small-01`
- `model-creature-tallow-ooze-puddle-01`
- `model-creature-tallow-ooze-frozen-01`
- `model-creature-mimic-book-01`
- `model-creature-mimic-lectern-01`
- `model-creature-mimic-chest-01`

## Scope
- In: Concept/reference prompt per id above
- In: Model output spec (tri budget, texture, bones) recorded in each prompt
- Out: 3D generation (`e37-asset-creatures-bestiary-3d-generate`)

## Notes
Ids use canon short names (world needs list said `creature-wolf-briar-01`, `creature-spider-loom-01`, `creature-sentinel-armour-01`, `creature-ooze-tallow-01`). Ooze puddle is a mesh decal state; the frozen variant is matte and cracked.

Budget: standard creature 2–6 k tris, LOD1 50 %, LOD2 20 %, T1 512², 1 material, ≤ 65 bones (style bible §13.2); ooze variants and mimics may be lighter (≤ 2 k). Prompts cite the locked style anchors from `e37-asset-style-lock`; canon names and details follow `docs/narrative/story-bible.md`.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the 7 concept ids, when the asset validator runs, then each has exactly one prompt file whose id equals its filename stem and passes naming checks.
- AC-2 [content] Given each prompt file, when compared with docs/art/style-bible.md §14 and §14.1, then the preamble and category add-on match byte-for-byte.
- AC-3 [content] Given each prompt file, when inspected, then it records the §13.2 model budget (standard creature 2–6 k tris, LOD1 50 %, LOD2 20 %, T1 512², 1 material, ≤ 65 bones (style bible §13.2); ooze variants and mimics may be lighter (≤ 2 k)) and the silhouette/palette rules from §5 relevant to the asset.
- AC-4 [content] Given the set, when reviewed against the bible, then every prompt spells out what the approval criterion needs: each creature's family shape (wedge, hollow rectangles, radial spikes, soft blob, box/slab) reads at 20 m, disposition cues read (wolf head up/down), the ooze reads as wax not element, and each mimic's tell is findable by an attentive player.
- AC-5 [content] Edge: given a prompt asking for perspective views, cast shadows or busy backgrounds that break image-to-3D, or containing text requests, a non-canon name or an API key pattern, when the validator runs, then it fails naming the file.

items.description:

The Forgotten's three-move set, crumble-and-reassemble and habit idles are how players learn to read and avoid them; Clatter's fidgets make him a person.

Miner three-move set (chop, 2-hit slash, lunge), collapse and reassemble, hauling idle; monk staff sweep, censer swing, sweeping and praying idles, a calm "settle" when the Vesper hymn is hummed; Clatter tending his mushrooms and an apologetic fidget.

- `anim-forgotten-lunge-01`

- `anim-forgotten-censer-swing-01`

items.title: Owner approval: Brother Horn animations
items.description:
## Why
Every shipped asset needs an owner decision at the animation gate; CI refuses final assets without one (contract §6).

## What
The owner reviews the 8 preview GIFs and approves or rejects each item with a note. Claude records every decision in `assets/approvals.json` (asset id, gate: animation, version, SHA-256, approver, date, notes). Rejected items loop back to `e37-asset-anim-horn-generate` with the note appended to their iteration log.

## Scope
- In: Owner decision per asset
- In: Approval records written by Claude
- In: Re-queue of rejected items
- Out: Generation or editing by the owner — the owner never edits assets

## Notes
Approval criteria: Horn reads nine feet tall and heavy, attacks read as stopping not killing, the yield reads as choice not defeat, and the carry is gentle. Batch reviews are designed to take ≤ 15 minutes of owner time.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the review page, when the owner finishes the session, then each of the 8 ids has an approve or reject decision with notes recorded in `assets/approvals.json` for gate "animation".
- AC-2 [manual] Given the approved items viewed side by side, when the owner compares them, then Horn reads nine feet tall and heavy, attacks read as stopping not killing, the yield reads as choice not defeat, and the carry is gentle.
- AC-3 [integration] Edge: given a rejected id, when its decision is recorded, then it is re-queued for `e37-asset-anim-horn-generate` with the owner note in its iteration log, and no already-approved id is regenerated.
- AC-4 [integration] Given an approval record whose SHA-256 does not match the file promoted to `assets/source/`, when CI runs, then the approval check fails naming the id.

items.title: Write main theme and motif anchor Suno prompts (3)
items.description:
## Why
Suno cannot reproduce a melody from text, so every derived track is built from approved motif anchors (audio bible §1.4); these three come first.

## What
Write one prompt file per track in `assets/prompts/music/<asset-id>.md` from `_templates/music-track.md`: Style field = SUNO STYLE PREAMBLE (audio bible §4.1) verbatim + tags, Exclude styles, structure-only Lyrics, key/mode, BPM, metre, length, loop plan and output spec.

The title main theme ("The Glen", D Dorian 84 BPM 6/8), the Vesper hymn motif anchor (D Dorian plainchant line answered by a low bell toll, free-time) and the Nightjar's song motif anchor (E Aeolian 3/4 lullaby that drifts out of tune over a churring trill).

Asset ids (3):
- `music-title-main-theme`
- `music-motif-vesper-hymn`
- `music-motif-nightjar-song`

## Scope
- In: One Suno prompt per id
- In: Motif references per audio bible §1.4 and family key/BPM per §3
- Out: Pasting into Suno (`e38-asset-music-anchors-generate`, owner)

## Notes
Anchors are used as Suno audio references for every other world music set; `music-hymn-vesper-hum` (diegetic hum) is derived from the hymn anchor in `e38-asset-music-stingers-world-*`.

Music is human-in-the-loop: the owner pastes each Suno prompt (≈ 1 min per track) and drops the chosen take in `assets/_incoming/music/`. Family members share key/mode and BPM (audio bible §2.2); derived tracks use the approved motif anchors as audio reference where the Suno tier allows. Not gated by the sonic lock (different medium). Paid Suno tier required for distribution.

items.title: Write Deepworks, priory and Knot ambience prompts (12 assets)
items.description:
## Why
Dungeon ambience is most of what the player hears (silence budget, audio bible §2.1) and it hides gameplay cues: draughts at weak walls, the song rising toward the Cradle.

## What
Write one prompt file per asset (or round-robin set) in `assets/prompts/sfx/<asset-id>.md` from `_templates/sfx.md`, with the SFX PREAMBLE (audio bible §8) verbatim, the category add-on, sourcing (generated vs CC0), round-robin count, sim link, output spec and checklist.

Deepworks drips, winch creaks, distant goblin camp; priory nave wind, scriptorium candles, belfry wind with the cracked bell's occasional hum; the Knot's hum, Ossuary bone rattles, Chapel of Echoes, the Fold's warm breathing (sleepers), Sounding Shaft updraft, and the Cradle dream bed carrying the Nightjar's song low and drifting.

Asset ids (12):
- `amb-deepworks-drips-01`
- `amb-deepworks-creaks-01`
- `amb-deepworks-goblin-camp-01`
- `amb-bellhollow-nave-wind-01`
- `amb-bellhollow-scriptorium-candles-01`
- `amb-bellhollow-belfry-wind-01`
- `amb-knot-hum-01`
- `amb-knot-ossuary-bones-01`
- `amb-knot-chapel-echoes-01`
- `amb-knot-fold-breathing-01`
- `amb-knot-sounding-shaft-updraft-01`
- `amb-knot-cradle-dream-01`

## Scope
- In: One prompt file per asset id above
- In: Sim link (surface id / noise radius / creature state / world fact) per sound
- Out: Generation (`e38-asset-amb-dungeon-generate`)

## Notes
Ids use canon location names (audio bible §6 example `amb-deepworks-drips-01`; the needs list said `amb-old-mine-*`, `amb-priory-*`, `amb-fold-*`, `amb-cradle-*`). The Cradle bed is built from the approved Nightjar motif anchor. Replaces part A placeholder `amb-placeholder-dungeon-drips-loop-01`.

Prompts cite the locked reference sounds from `e38-asset-sonic-lock`. Canon names follow `docs/narrative/story-bible.md`; no intelligible speech anywhere (text-only MVP).
items.acceptance:

items.description:
## Why
Every shipped asset needs an owner decision at the sfx batch gate; CI refuses final assets without one (contract §6).

## What
The owner reviews the listening page of 12 sounds and approves or rejects each item with a note. items.title: Write Hushling and abbot SFX prompts (8 assets)
items.description:
## Why
Hushlings hunt by sound and mimic the missing; the abbot is gentle presence until he sings — both are the dread the audio bible asks for, quiet and specific.

## What
Write one prompt file per asset (or round-robin set) in `assets/prompts/sfx/<asset-id>.md` from `_templates/sfx.md`, with the SFX PREAMBLE (audio bible §8) verbatim, the category add-on, sourcing (generated vs CC0), round-robin count, sim link, output spec and checklist.

Hushling whisper-grasp, dissipation (ripping air scattering into whispers), idle hum loop of the Nightjar's song, and the voice-mimic murmur (pitch-contoured, fog-filtered, familiar intonation, no intelligible words; the line appears as a caption); the abbot's sung Nightjar fragment loop (warm wordless male voice, solid state), interrupted-song cut, lantern-chain creak loop, and fog hush loop.

Asset ids (8):
- `sfx-creature-hushling-whisper-grasp-01`
- `sfx-creature-hushling-dissipate-01`
- `sfx-creature-hushling-idle-hum-loop-01`
- `sfx-creature-hushling-mimic-01`
- `sfx-creature-abbot-sing-loop-01`
- `sfx-creature-abbot-interrupt-01`
- `sfx-creature-abbot-lantern-chain-loop-01`
- `sfx-creature-abbot-fog-hush-loop-01`

## Scope
- In: One prompt file per asset id above
- In: Sim link (surface id / noise radius / creature state / world fact) per sound
- Out: Generation (`e38-asset-sfx-creatures-dream-generate`)

## Notes
Ids follow audio bible §6 (`sfx-creature-hushling-mimic-01` is the bible example). Sung/hummed fragments are built from the Nightjar motif anchor.

Prompts cite the locked reference sounds from `e38-asset-sonic-lock`. Canon names follow `docs/narrative/story-bible.md`; no intelligible speech anywhere (text-only MVP).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the 8 asset ids, when the asset validator runs over `assets/prompts/sfx/`, then each has exactly one prompt file whose id equals its filename stem and matches audio bible §6 naming.
- AC-2 [content] Given each prompt file, when the validator compares its preamble with docs/audio/audio-bible.md §8, then it matches byte-for-byte.
- AC-3 [content] Given each repeated sound, when inspected, then its round-robin count is ≥ 3 (footsteps 4–6) and its sim link names the sim id it must match.
- AC-4 [content] Given each prompt file, when inspected, then it states duration, mono/stereo, loop yes/no and loudness target from audio bible §5.1 (SFX one-shots peak −3 dBFS, ≤ −1.0 dBTP).
- AC-5 [content] Edge: given a prompt that requests intelligible speech, music (unless the bible names a diegetic melody), or contains an API key pattern, when the validator runs, then it fails naming the file.
